title: Mexican Street Corn Ramen
description: Rich miso ramen topped with charred elote-style corn, lime mayo, crumbled feta, chilli and fresh coriander for a bowl full of street-food flavour.
steps: Cook the eggs: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then cool them in cold water and peel.
Char the corn: Rub the corn with butter and roast it in a hot griddle pan for 8 minutes, turning, until charred in spots. Cut the kernels off the cobs.
Make the broth: Heat the stock with the grated garlic, then take it off the boil and whisk in the miso.
Cook the noodles: Cook the ramen noodles for 2-3 minutes and drain.
Assemble the bowls: Divide noodles and broth between bowls and top with corn, halved eggs, crumbled feta, lime mayo (mayonnaise mixed with lime juice), chilli powder and coriander.

title: Wild Mushroom Velouté
description: A velvety, deeply earthy soup of wild mushrooms and porcini, enriched with cream and a splash of sherry, topped with crisp sautéed mushrooms and chives.
steps: Soak the porcini: Cover the dried porcini with 200 ml boiling water and leave them to soak for 15 minutes, then chop them and keep the soaking liquid.
Sauté the mushrooms: Fry the sliced wild mushrooms in half the butter over high heat until golden, then set aside a handful for the garnish.
Cook the aromatics: Add the remaining butter, chopped onion, garlic and thyme leaves and cook gently for 5 minutes until soft.
Simmer the soup: Pour in the sherry and let it bubble for a minute, then add the porcini, strained soaking liquid and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend until silky: Blend the soup until completely smooth, return it to the pan, stir in the cream and season to taste.
Serve: Ladle into warm bowls and top with the reserved mushrooms and snipped chives.

title: Yakisoba (Stir-fried Noodles)
description: Smoky street-food style stir-fried noodles tossed with crispy pork belly, cabbage and carrot in a tangy-sweet homemade yakisoba sauce, topped with red ginger and aonori.
steps: Mix the sauce: Stir the Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, soy sauce and sugar together in a small bowl.
Prepare pork and vegetables: Cut the pork belly into 4 cm pieces, slice the onion, cut the carrot into thin matchsticks and the cabbage into bite-size squares.
Loosen the noodles: Rinse the noodles briefly under hot water and gently pull them apart with your fingers.
Fry the pork: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat and fry the pork for 3 minutes until crisp.
Stir-fry the vegetables: Add the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the cabbage and cook for 2 more minutes until just wilted.
Toss the noodles: Add the noodles with 2 tbsp water and toss for 2 minutes, then pour in the sauce and toss until everything is evenly coated and slightly charred.
Serve: Pile the yakisoba onto plates and top with pickled red ginger and a sprinkle of aonori.

title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
description: Hunter-style chicken thighs braised with peppers, mushrooms, tomatoes, rosemary and olives in white wine, served over soft, creamy polenta.
steps: Season the chicken: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and dust them lightly with flour.
Slice the vegetables: Slice the onion, cut the pepper into strips, quarter the mushrooms and chop the garlic.
Brown the chicken: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large casserole and brown the chicken skin side down until golden, then turn and brown briefly. Set aside.
Sauté the vegetables: Fry the onion, pepper, mushrooms and garlic in the same pot for about 8 minutes until softened.
Braise the chicken: Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, add the tomatoes and rosemary, return the chicken and simmer covered for 35 minutes.
Cook the polenta: Bring the water to the boil with a pinch of salt, whisk in the polenta and stir for 5-8 minutes until thick. Stir in the remaining olive oil and keep warm.
Add the olives: Uncover, add the olives and let the sauce reduce for 5 minutes. Remove the rosemary sprigs.
Serve: Spoon the polenta onto plates and top with the chicken and sauce.

title: Dampfnudeln with Vanilla Sauce
description: Fluffy steamed yeast dumplings with a sticky caramelised crust on the bottom, served warm in a pool of homemade vanilla sauce - a much-loved Palatinate sweet meal.
steps: Make the yeast dough: Warm 200 ml milk until lukewarm. Knead it with the flour, yeast, 50 g sugar, 1 egg, 50 g butter and the salt for 8-10 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough.
Let it rise: Cover the bowl and leave the dough in a warm place for about 45 minutes until doubled in size.
Shape the dumplings: Divide the dough into 8 pieces, roll them into smooth balls and let them rise again under a tea towel for 20 minutes.

Make the vanilla sauce: While the dumplings rise, heat 500 ml milk with the scraped vanilla pod and 40 g sugar. Whisk 2 egg yolks with the cornflour and a little cold milk, stir into the hot milk and cook, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Steam the Dampfnudeln: Heat 150 ml milk, 30 g butter and 10 g sugar in a wide pan with a tight lid. Place the balls in, cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Crisp the bottoms: When you hear a crackling sound the liquid is gone and a caramel crust is forming. Remove the lid and let the dumplings steam off for a moment.
Serve: Serve the warm Dampfnudeln crust side up with the vanilla sauce.

title: Rajma Masala
description: Hearty red kidney beans simmered in a thick, tangy onion and tomato gravy with cumin and warming spices, the Punjabi comfort food traditionally served with rice.
steps: Prepare the ingredients: Rinse and drain the kidney beans and finely chop the onions. Blend the tomatoes with the garlic, ginger and green chili into a purée.
Fry the onions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the cumin seeds and bay leaves, then fry the onions for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Cook the masala: Add the tomato purée, ground coriander and chili powder and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Simmer the beans: Add the beans and 400 ml water, mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy and simmer for 15 minutes.
Finish and serve: Stir in the garam masala, season with salt and serve hot with steamed basmati rice.

title: Tuna Tartare with Avocado
description: Finely diced sushi-grade tuna dressed with soy, sesame, lime and ginger, layered over creamy avocado for a fresh and elegant no-cook starter.
steps: Dice the tuna: Using a very sharp knife, cut the chilled tuna into 5 mm cubes and keep it cold in a bowl set over ice.
Make the dressing: Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil, the juice of half the lime, grated ginger and very finely chopped shallot.
Prepare the avocado: Dice the avocado, toss it with the remaining lime juice and season with a little salt.
Dress the tuna: Fold the dressing and most of the chopped chives into the tuna just before serving, and season with pepper.
Plate: Press the avocado into a ring mould on each plate, top with the tuna and lift off the ring. Garnish with sesame seeds and the remaining chives.

title: Chocolate Fondant
description: Warm individual chocolate cakes with a crisp outside and a molten, gooey centre that flows onto the plate, the dessert restaurant chefs love to serve.
steps: Prepare the moulds: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Brush 4 dariole moulds with a little of the butter, chill them for 5 minutes, then dust with cocoa powder and tap out the excess.
Melt chocolate and butter: Melt the chopped chocolate and remaining butter in a bowl over simmering water, stirring until smooth, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs: Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, sugar and salt for about 5 minutes until thick, pale and doubled in volume.
Combine the batter: Fold the chocolate mixture into the eggs, then sift in the flour and fold gently until just combined. Divide the batter between the moulds.
Bake: Bake for 10-12 minutes until the tops are firm and have risen but the centres still wobble when shaken.
Turn out and serve: Leave for 1 minute, run a knife around the edges and turn the fondants out onto plates. Serve immediately with vanilla ice cream.

title: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
description: Irresistibly crunchy, double-fried chicken thigh bites marinated in soy, garlic and ginger, served with lemon wedges and Japanese mayonnaise for dipping.
steps: Cut the chicken: Cut the chicken thighs into 4 cm pieces, leaving the skin on for extra crunch.
Marinate the chicken: Grate the garlic and ginger and mix with soy sauce, sake, sugar and a pinch of salt. Toss the chicken in the marinade and chill it for 30 minutes.
Prepare oil and garnish: In the last 10 minutes of marinating, heat the oil in a deep pot to 160 °C and cut the lemon into wedges.
Coat the chicken: Drain the chicken briefly, toss the pieces in the potato starch and shake off any excess.
First fry: Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until pale golden, then rest it on a wire rack for 4 minutes so the heat carries through.
Second fry: Raise the oil to 180 °C and fry the chicken again for 1 minute until deep golden and extra crunchy. Drain on the rack.
Serve: Serve the karaage hot with lemon wedges and Japanese mayonnaise on the side.

title: Strammer Max
description: Buttery toasted farmhouse bread piled with warm ham and a runny fried egg, served with gherkins and tomatoes - the classic German pub snack ready in minutes.
steps: Toast the bread: Spread the bread thinly with half the butter and toast it butter side down in a large pan until golden. Transfer to plates.
Warm the ham: Briefly warm the ham slices in the pan, then fold them onto the toasted bread.
Fry the eggs: Melt the remaining butter and fry the eggs sunny side up over medium heat until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Assemble: Slide one egg onto each slice, season with salt and pepper and scatter with chopped chives.
Serve: Serve straight away with sliced gherkins and tomatoes on the side.

title: Black Truffle Risotto
description: Creamy Carnaroli risotto enriched with butter and aged cheese, finished with fragrant truffle oil and freshly shaved black truffle for a truly indulgent dish.
steps: Heat the stock: Bring the vegetable stock to a gentle simmer in a saucepan and keep it hot next to the stove.
Toast the rice: Soften the finely chopped shallot in the olive oil for 3 minutes, then add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains turn glassy.
Deglaze with wine: Pour in the white wine and stir until it has been completely absorbed.
Add the stock gradually: Add the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is absorbed. Cook for 17-18 minutes until the rice is creamy but still al dente.
Beat in butter and cheese: Take the pan off the heat, beat in the cold butter, grated cheese and truffle oil and season to taste. Cover and let it rest for 2 minutes.
Shave the truffle: Spoon the risotto onto warm plates and shave the black truffle generously over the top just before serving.

title: Penne all'Arrabbiata
description: Fiery Roman penne in a garlicky tomato sauce spiked with dried red chilli, finished with fresh parsley for a quick and punchy weeknight dinner.
steps: Boil the water: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add most of the salt.
Fry garlic and chilli: Gently fry the sliced garlic and crumbled chillies in the olive oil until fragrant but not brown.
Simmer sauce and cook pasta: Add the tomatoes, crush them with a spoon, season and simmer for 10 minutes. Meanwhile cook the penne 1 minute less than the packet says.
Toss together: Drain the penne, add it to the sauce with a splash of pasta water and toss over high heat for 1 minute.
Serve: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve hot.

title: Katsu Sando
description: Crispy panko-crusted pork cutlets with tangy tonkatsu sauce and finely shredded cabbage, pressed between pillowy crustless milk bread.
steps: Prep the cabbage: Shred the cabbage as finely as possible and keep it in cold water so it stays crisp.
Bread the cutlets: Pound the cutlets to an even 1.5 cm, season with salt and coat in flour, beaten egg and then panko.
Fry the cutlets: Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170 °C and fry the cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Drain and rest for 3 minutes.
Build the sandwiches: Spread 4 bread slices with mayonnaise, add drained cabbage, a cutlet brushed with tonkatsu sauce and the remaining bread.
Cut and serve: Press gently, trim off the crusts and cut each sandwich in half to show the crispy cutlet.

title: Malai Kofta
description: Soft, golden potato and paneer dumplings served in a luxurious, lightly sweet tomato and cashew cream sauce, a rich vegetarian dish for special occasions.
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 20 minutes until tender, then drain, peel and let them steam dry.
Start the sauce: Soak the cashews in hot water. Chop the onions and fry them in the ghee for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Simmer the gravy: Add the tomatoes, chili powder, half the garam masala, sugar and drained cashews and simmer for 15 minutes. Blend until completely smooth.
Shape the koftas: Mash the potatoes, grate in the paneer and mix with the cornstarch, salt and remaining garam masala. Shape into 12 smooth balls with no cracks.
Fry the koftas: Heat the frying oil to about 170°C and fry the koftas in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Finish the sauce: Return the blended gravy to the pan, stir in the cream, season with salt and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Assemble and serve: Place the koftas in a serving dish and pour the hot sauce over them just before serving so they stay soft but intact.

title: Maki Sushi (Cucumber and Avocado Rolls)
description: Neat homemade sushi rolls of seasoned vinegar rice and crisp nori filled with fresh cucumber and creamy avocado, served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.
steps: Rinse and cook the rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and let it drain for 10 minutes. Cook it with the water in a covered pot on low heat for 13 minutes, then rest it covered for 10 minutes.
Make the sushi vinegar: Warm the rice vinegar with the sugar and salt, stirring until dissolved, then let it cool.
Cut the fillings: Halve the cucumber lengthwise, scrape out the seeds and cut it into long thin sticks. Halve, stone and slice the avocados.
Season the rice: Tip the hot rice into a wide bowl, pour over the sushi vinegar and fold it in with cutting motions while fanning, until glossy and at body temperature.

Roll the cucumber maki: Place half a nori sheet shiny side down on a bamboo mat, spread a thin layer of rice over it with wet hands leaving a 1 cm border, lay cucumber along the edge and roll up tightly.
Roll the avocado maki: At the same time, roll the remaining nori halves the same way with avocado slices and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Slice and serve: Cut each roll into 6 pieces with a sharp knife wiped with a damp cloth between cuts. Serve with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

title: Rack of Lamb with Herb Crust
description: Juicy, pink-roasted rack of lamb coated in a vibrant crust of fresh herbs, garlic and mustard, served with crisp roast potatoes and green beans.
steps: Prepare the lamb: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Trim excess fat from the racks, season them well and let them come to room temperature.
Roast the potatoes: Halve the baby potatoes, toss them with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt and roast on a tray for 35 minutes until golden.
Sear the racks: Sear the lamb fat-side down in a hot pan with a little oil, then briefly on all other sides until browned.
Make the herb crust: Blitz the breadcrumbs, parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic and 2 tbsp olive oil in a food processor to a vibrant green crumb.
Coat and roast: Brush the fat side of the racks with mustard, press the herb crumb firmly on top and roast for 18-20 minutes for pink meat.
Blanch the beans: Cook the green beans in salted boiling water for 4-5 minutes, drain and toss with the remaining olive oil.

title: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant mashed and cooked with onions, tomatoes, garlic and green chilies into a rustic, deeply flavourful Punjabi dish.

Chop the vegetables: Finely chop the onions, tomatoes, garlic, green chilies and fresh coriander.
Cook the masala: Heat the remaining oil, sizzle the cumin seeds and fry the onions for 7 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger and chilies, then the tomatoes and chili powder, and cook until soft.
Peel and mash: Let the eggplants cool slightly, peel away the charred skin and mash the smoky flesh with a fork.
Combine and cook: Add the mashed eggplant to the masala and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until thick. Season with salt.

title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Rome's famously simple pasta, where Pecorino, toasted black pepper and starchy cooking water come together into an irresistibly creamy, peppery sauce.
steps: Boil the water: Bring a pot of water to the boil, using a little less than usual so it gets starchy, and salt it lightly because Pecorino is salty.
Toast the pepper: Crush the peppercorns coarsely and toast them in a dry, wide pan for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the butter.
Make the cheese paste: Finely grate both cheeses and mix them with a few tablespoons of cold water to a thick paste.
Cook the pasta: Cook the pasta until just short of al dente and keep plenty of the cooking water.
Emulsify: Move the pasta to the pepper pan with a ladle of cooking water and toss. Off the heat, add the cheese paste loosened with a little more water and toss vigorously until creamy.
Serve: Serve immediately with a little extra Pecorino and pepper.

title: Onigiri (Salmon Rice Balls)
description: Classic triangular rice balls filled with flaky soy-seasoned grilled salmon and sesame, wrapped in crisp nori and perfect for lunch boxes or picnics.
steps: Rinse and soak the rice: Rinse the rice 3 to 4 times until the water runs almost clear, then soak it in the measured water for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice: Bring the rice to the boil in its soaking water, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 13 minutes. Rest it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Cook the salmon: While the rice cooks, salt the salmon and pan-fry it for 4 minutes on each side. Flake it, removing skin and bones, and mix with the soy sauce and sesame seeds.
Cool the rice slightly: Spread the rice out in a wide bowl for a few minutes until it is warm but comfortable to touch.
Shape the onigiri: Wet your hands and rub them with a little salt. Take an eighth of the rice, press a hollow into it, add some salmon, cover with rice and press it into a triangle.
Wrap in nori: Cut the nori sheets in half and wrap one strip around the base of each onigiri. Serve straight away or wrap tightly in cling film for later.

Prep the salad: Shred the lettuce, slice the tomatoes, the rest of the cucumber and the red onion.
Cook the chicken: Fry the chicken in the oil over high heat for 6-8 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the wraps: Heat the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side.
Roll the wraps: Fill each tortilla with salad, chicken and a spoonful of raita, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Cut in half to serve.

title: Vegetable Korma
description: Mixed garden vegetables gently simmered in a mild, creamy cashew and yogurt sauce scented with cardamom, an elegant and family-friendly vegetarian curry.

Blend the cashew paste: Drain the cashews and blend them with the yogurt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Sauté the aromatics: Heat the ghee in a large pan, add the cardamom pods and onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add the vegetables: Add the ground coriander, carrots, beans and cauliflower and stir for 2 minutes so the vegetables are coated in the spices.
Simmer the korma: Stir in the cashew paste and 200 ml water, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender, adding the peas for the last 5 minutes.

title: Sukiyaki (Beef Hot Pot)
description: A festive one-pan hot pot of thinly sliced beef, tofu, mushrooms and vegetables simmered in a sweet soy broth, traditionally dipped into beaten egg at the table.
steps: Make the warishita: Heat soy sauce, mirin, sake, 2 tbsp sugar and the water in a small pan until the sugar dissolves, then set aside.
Prepare the vegetables: Slice the leek diagonally, cut the cabbage into wide pieces, cut a cross into each shiitake cap and trim the enoki into small bunches.
Prepare tofu and noodles: Cut the tofu into large cubes. Rinse the shirataki, blanch for 2 minutes in boiling water, drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Sear the beef: Heat the oil in a wide cast-iron pan, add a few slices of beef, sprinkle with the remaining sugar and a splash of warishita and cook briefly until just browned.
Arrange and simmer: Arrange the vegetables, tofu and shirataki in sections around the beef, pour in the warishita and simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Prepare the dipping eggs: Meanwhile crack one very fresh egg into each of four small bowls and beat it lightly with chopsticks.
Add the rest of the beef: Lay the remaining beef on top, cook for 1 to 2 minutes until just pink, then bring the pan to the table and let everyone dip their pieces into the egg.

title: Kartoffelpuffer with Homemade Apple Sauce

Grate the potatoes: Peel the potatoes and onion and grate them finely. Put the mixture in a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the batter: Mix the grated potatoes and onion with the eggs, flour, salt and nutmeg.
Fry the pancakes: Heat a generous layer of oil in a large pan. Add heaped tablespoons of batter, flatten them and fry in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Keep them warm: Drain the finished pancakes on kitchen paper and keep them warm in a 100 °C oven while the rest are frying.
Serve: Serve the hot Kartoffelpuffer with the apple sauce on the side.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
description: Creamy golden saffron risotto from Milan, slowly stirred with white wine and stock, then finished with cold butter and Parmigiano.
steps: Heat the stock: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer and steep the saffron in a ladle of hot stock.
Soften the onion: Melt half the butter with the oil and gently cook the finely chopped onion for 4-5 minutes without browning.
Toast the rice: Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the edges turn translucent, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.

Add the stock gradually: Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until it is absorbed before adding more. After 10 minutes stir in the saffron stock and cook for about 18 minutes in total.
Finish the risotto: Take the pot off the heat, beat in the remaining cold butter and the grated Parmigiano, season with salt and rest covered for 2 minutes.
Serve: Spread the risotto on warm plates; it should flow gently like a wave.

title: Filet Mignon with Béarnaise Sauce
description: Perfectly seared beef fillet steaks crowned with silky homemade béarnaise, the buttery tarragon sauce that turns a simple steak into a true steakhouse classic.
steps: Temper the steaks: Pat the steaks dry, season them generously and let them come to room temperature while the sauce is prepared.
Make the reduction: Simmer the chopped shallots, vinegar, wine, crushed peppercorns and half the tarragon until only about 2 tablespoons of liquid remain, then strain.
Clarify the butter: Melt the butter gently and skim off the foam so you have clear, warm butter for the sauce.

Whisk the béarnaise: Whisk the egg yolks with the reduction in a bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale. Slowly drizzle in the warm butter while whisking, then add the remaining tarragon and a pinch of salt.
Sear the steaks: Heat the oil in a heavy pan until smoking and sear the steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, spooning the pan juices over them.
Rest and serve: Rest the steaks for 5 minutes, then plate them with a generous spoonful of béarnaise on top.

title: Masala Dosa

title: Miso Butter Pasta
description: Spaghetti coated in a glossy, deeply savoury sauce of white miso, butter and garlic, finished with Parmesan, black pepper and fresh spring onions.
steps: Cook the pasta: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, then keep a cup of the pasta water before draining.
Make the miso butter: While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a large pan and gently fry the sliced garlic for 2 minutes. Whisk in the miso with a splash of pasta water until smooth.
Toss the pasta: Add the drained spaghetti and half the Parmesan to the pan and toss with more pasta water until glossy and silky.

title: Crème Brûlée
description: Silky vanilla custard baked gently in a water bath and finished with a crackling layer of caramelised sugar, the most famous dessert of French fine dining.
steps: Infuse the cream: Preheat the oven to 150 °C. Split the vanilla pod, scrape out the seeds and heat both with the cream until just steaming, then let it infuse for 5 minutes.
Mix the custard: Whisk the egg yolks with the caster sugar and salt until pale, then slowly pour in the warm cream while stirring. Strain the mixture and skim off any foam.

Bake in a water bath: Pour the custard into 4 shallow ramekins set in a deep tray and fill the tray with hot water halfway up the sides. Bake for 30-35 minutes until set but still slightly wobbly in the centre.
Chill: Let the ramekins cool, then chill them in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Caramelise the top: Sprinkle an even layer of demerara sugar over each custard and melt it with a kitchen blowtorch until deep amber. Wait 2 minutes for the caramel to harden, then serve.

title: Yakitori (Negima Chicken Skewers)
description: Smoky grilled chicken and spring onion skewers brushed again and again with a sticky, sweet-savoury tare sauce until beautifully lacquered and caramelised.
steps: Soak the skewers: Place the bamboo skewers in a tray of water for at least 30 minutes so they do not burn on the grill.
Make the tare sauce: Simmer soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar in a small pan for 10 to 12 minutes until reduced by a third and syrupy. Pour a third into a serving bowl.
Cut chicken and spring onions: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and the white and pale green parts of the spring onions into 3 cm lengths.
Thread the skewers: Thread chicken and spring onion pieces alternately onto the soaked skewers, using about four pieces of chicken per skewer.
Heat the grill: Preheat a grill or ridged grill pan over high heat and brush it lightly with the oil.
Grill the skewers: Season the skewers lightly with salt and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until the chicken is almost cooked through.
Glaze with tare: Brush the skewers with the sauce from the pan three times, grilling for about 1 minute between coats until glossy and caramelised.
Serve: Sprinkle the skewers with shichimi togarashi and serve with the reserved tare for dipping.

title: Punjabi Samosas
description: Crisp, flaky pastry pyramids filled with spiced potatoes and green peas, fried until golden and best enjoyed hot with tamarind or mint chutney.
steps: Make the dough: Mix the flour, carom seeds and a pinch of salt, then rub in 4 tbsp oil until crumbly. Add the water gradually to form a stiff dough, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 20 minutes until tender. Drain, peel and crumble them roughly.
Cook the filling: Heat 1 tbsp oil, sizzle the cumin seeds, then add ginger, chopped chili and peas for 2 minutes. Stir in the potatoes, garam masala, amchur and salt, mash lightly and let it cool.
Roll the pastry: Divide the rested dough into 6 balls, roll each into a thin oval and cut it in half. Shape each half into a cone and seal the seam with a little water.
Fill and seal: Fill each cone with the cooled potato mixture, then moisten the top edge and pinch it firmly closed.
Heat the oil: Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to about 160°C, which is when a small piece of dough rises slowly to the surface.
Fry the samosas: Fry the samosas in batches over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper and serve warm.

title: Tiramisù
description: The beloved Venetian dessert of espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with a light, airy mascarpone cream and finished with a dusting of cocoa.
steps: Make the coffee: Brew the espresso, stir in the Marsala and let it cool completely in a shallow dish.
Whisk yolks and sugar: Beat the egg yolks with the sugar for about 5 minutes until pale and thick.
Fold in the mascarpone: Stir the mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
Beat the egg whites: Whisk the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the cream.
Dip and layer: Dip each ladyfinger briefly into the coffee and lay them in a dish. Cover with half the cream, then repeat with a second layer.
Chill: Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, so the layers set.
Dust and serve: Dust generously with cocoa powder just before serving.

title: Banh Mi Burger

Mix the patties: Finely chop the lemongrass and mix it with the pork, fish sauce and a little grated ginger. Shape four patties slightly wider than the buns and chill for 10 minutes.
Prep the toppings: Slice the cucumber and jalapeño thinly, pick the coriander and stir sriracha into the mayonnaise.
Cook the patties: Fry the patties in the oil over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through.
Toast the buns: Toast the brioche buns cut side down in a dry pan until golden.
Assemble the burgers: Spread the buns with sriracha mayo and layer patty, drained pickles, cucumber, jalapeño and coriander. Serve immediately.

title: Swabian Maultaschen in Broth
description: Hand-made pasta pockets filled with seasoned pork, spinach and herbs, gently simmered and served in a clear, steaming beef broth with fresh chives.
steps: Make the pasta dough: Knead the flour, 2 eggs, 2 tbsp water and a pinch of salt into a smooth, firm dough. Wrap it and let it rest for 30 minutes.

Prepare the filling: Soak the roll in water and squeeze it out. Soften the diced onion in the butter, blanch and finely chop the spinach, then mix everything with the pork, 1 egg, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat the broth: While the dough rests, bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a wide pot.
Roll out the dough: Roll the dough out very thinly on a floured surface into two long strips about 12 cm wide.
Fill and shape: Spread the filling along one half of each strip, fold the dough over and press down firmly every 8 cm with the handle of a wooden spoon. Cut into pockets and seal the edges well.
Simmer the Maultaschen: Slide the pockets into the barely simmering broth and cook for 15 minutes without boiling, so they stay intact.
Serve: Serve the Maultaschen in deep bowls with plenty of broth, sprinkled with chopped chives.

title: Lobster Thermidor
description: Luxurious lobster meat folded into a creamy mustard, tarragon and white wine sauce, spooned back into the shells and grilled until bubbling and golden.
steps: Split the lobsters: Preheat the grill. Cut the lobsters in half lengthwise with a heavy knife, remove the meat from tails and claws and cut it into bite-size pieces, keeping the cleaned shells.
Reduce wine and stock: Melt half the butter and soften the finely chopped shallot, then add the wine and fish stock and boil until reduced to about a third.
Make the sauce: Stir in the cream and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes until thick. Off the heat, whisk in the egg yolk, chopped tarragon, a squeeze of lemon, half the cheese and seasoning.
Warm the lobster: Toss the lobster meat in the remaining butter just until warm, then fold it into the sauce.
Fill the shells: Spoon the mixture into the lobster shells, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and place them on a baking tray.
Grill until golden: Grill for 4-5 minutes until bubbling and golden brown, then serve at once with lemon wedges.

title: Yasai Tempura (Vegetable Tempura)
description: Feather-light, crackling tempura of sweet potato, courgette, shiitake and bell pepper, served with a warm tentsuyu dipping sauce and freshly grated daikon.
steps: Make the tentsuyu: Simmer the kombu dashi, soy sauce and mirin for 2 minutes and keep warm. Finely grate the daikon and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Cut the vegetables: Slice the sweet potato into 5 mm rounds, the courgette into diagonal slices and the pepper into wide strips, and trim the shiitake. Pat everything completely dry.
Heat the oil: Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 175 °C and set a wire rack over a tray next to it.
Mix the batter: Just before frying, whisk the egg with the ice-cold sparkling water, then add the flour and cornstarch and stir only briefly with chopsticks. A few lumps are fine.
Fry in small batches: Dip the vegetables into the batter, let the excess drip off and fry a few pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, or 4 minutes for sweet potato, until crisp and pale golden.
Drain and keep warm: Move each fried batch onto the rack, sprinkle with a little salt and keep warm in a 90 °C oven while the rest is fried.
Serve: Serve the tempura straight away with small bowls of tentsuyu and a mound of grated daikon to stir into the sauce.

title: Bulgogi Cheesesteak
description: Philly meets Seoul: thin slices of soy-and-pear marinated beef, caramelised onions and melted provolone piled into toasted hoagie rolls.

Caramelise the onions: Slice the onions and pepper and cook them slowly in the vegetable oil over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Toast the rolls: Split the rolls, spread with butter and toast them cut side down in a pan until golden.
Sear the beef: Fry the beef over high heat in batches for 2-3 minutes, then mix in the onions and peppers.
Melt the cheese: Divide the beef into four piles in the pan, lay two provolone slices on each and cover for 1 minute until melted.
Fill the rolls: Slide each cheesy pile into a toasted roll with a spatula and serve hot.

description: Pillowy homemade potato gnocchi tossed in a simple garlic and tomato sauce with fresh basil and a generous shower of Parmigiano.

Make the sauce: Gently fry the sliced garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and simmer for 15-20 minutes. Season and add torn basil.
Rice the potatoes: Peel the potatoes while hot and press them through a potato ricer onto a floured surface. Let the steam escape for 5 minutes.
Form the dough: Add the egg, a pinch of salt and most of the flour and knead briefly into a soft dough. Do not overwork it.

Boil the water: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and grate the Parmigiano.
Cook the gnocchi: Cook the gnocchi in batches and lift them out with a slotted spoon about 1 minute after they float to the top.
Toss and serve: Toss the gnocchi gently in the warm tomato sauce and serve with Parmigiano and basil.

title: Tandoori Chicken

title: Bavarian Schweinshaxe with Dark Beer Gravy
description: Slow-roasted pork knuckles with juicy, tender meat and a wonderfully crackling crust, served with a rich dark beer gravy - pure Munich beer garden feeling at home.
steps: Season the knuckles: Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Score the rind in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife and rub the knuckles well with salt, pepper, crushed caraway and crushed garlic.
Prepare the tin: Roughly chop the onions, carrots and celeriac and spread them in a roasting tin. Sit the knuckles on top, rind side down, and pour in the stock.
Slow roast: Roast for 1 1/2 hours, basting the meat with the juices every now and then.
Roast with beer: Turn the knuckles rind side up, pour the dark beer into the tin and roast for another hour, adding a splash of water if the tin gets dry.
Crisp the crackling: Raise the oven to 220 °C, or switch on the grill, and roast for 15-20 minutes until the rind puffs up and crackles. Watch closely so it does not burn.
Make the gravy: Strain the roasting juices into a small pan, skim off the excess fat and thicken with the cornflour mixed with a little cold water. Season to taste.
Serve: Cut the knuckles in half and serve with the dark beer gravy, ideally with potato dumplings and sauerkraut.

title: Miso Soup (Miso Shiru)
description: A soothing classic miso soup with a delicate kombu and shiitake broth, silky tofu cubes, tender wakame and fresh spring onions, ready in twenty minutes.
steps: Make the kombu dashi: Put the kombu and dried shiitake into the water in a pot and heat it slowly for about 8 minutes. Remove the kombu just before the water boils.
Soak the wakame: While the dashi heats, soak the wakame in a small bowl of cold water for 5 minutes, then drain it.
Prepare tofu and garnish: Cut the tofu into 1.5 cm cubes, lift out and slice the softened shiitake and thinly slice the spring onions.

title: Thai Green Curry Risotto

Cook the risotto: Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each is absorbed, for about 12 minutes.

title: Königsberger Klopse in Creamy Caper Sauce

Shape the meatballs: Knead the mince with the roll, onion, egg, salt and pepper until well combined. With wet hands shape 12 even balls.
Poach the Klopse: Bring the stock and bay leaves to a gentle simmer, add the meatballs and poach for 15 minutes without boiling. Lift them out and keep 600 ml of the stock.

title: Lamb Rogan Josh
description: Kashmiri slow-braised lamb in a deep red, aromatic sauce of yogurt, fennel, cardamom and mild Kashmiri chili, meltingly tender and richly warming.
steps: Cut the lamb: Cut the lamb into 3 to 4 cm chunks, pat them dry with kitchen paper and season with salt.
Prepare the aromatics: Finely slice the onions and crush the garlic. Whisk the yogurt with the chili powder and ground fennel until smooth.
Brown the lamb: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the lamb in batches for about 3 minutes per batch. Set the meat aside.
Fry onions and spices: In the same pot, fry the cardamom and cinnamon for 30 seconds, then add the onions and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the yogurt: Lower the heat and stir in the spiced yogurt one spoonful at a time so it does not curdle, then return the lamb and its juices to the pot.
Braise the lamb: Pour in the water, cover and simmer very gently for 75 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Finish the curry: Stir in the garam masala, adjust the salt and remove the cinnamon stick before serving.

title: Parmigiana di Melanzane
description: Golden fried aubergine slices layered with rich tomato sauce, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil, baked into a bubbling southern Italian classic.
steps: Salt the aubergines: Cut the aubergines lengthwise into 1 cm slices, sprinkle with salt and leave in a colander for 30 minutes.
Make the tomato sauce: Soften the chopped onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil, add the passata and simmer for 20 minutes. Season and stir in a few torn basil leaves.
Fry the aubergines: Pat the slices dry and fry them in batches in the remaining oil until golden on both sides. Drain on kitchen paper.
Prepare the cheese: Slice the mozzarella and let it drain, grate the Parmigiano and preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Layer: Spread sauce in a baking dish, then layer aubergine, sauce, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil. Repeat and finish with sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake: Bake for about 35 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.
Rest: Let the parmigiana rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the layers set.

title: Bouillabaisse
description: The famous Marseille fish stew: fragrant saffron and fennel broth filled with tender fish, prawns and mussels, served with garlicky rouille croutons.
steps: Start the broth: Heat half the olive oil in a wide pot and gently cook the sliced onion, fennel and two chopped garlic cloves for 10 minutes until soft.
Simmer with saffron: Add the tomatoes, most of the saffron and the fish stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare the seafood: Cut the fish into large chunks, peel and devein the prawns, and scrub and debeard the mussels, discarding any that stay open.

Make rouille and croutons: Stir one crushed garlic clove, the remaining saffron and a little olive oil into the mayonnaise. Rub the baguette slices with the last garlic clove, drizzle with oil and toast until golden.
Poach the seafood: Add the firmest fish to the simmering broth first, then the delicate pieces, prawns and mussels. Cover and cook gently for 6-8 minutes until the mussels open.
Serve: Ladle the broth and seafood into warm bowls and serve with the croutons topped with rouille.

title: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
description: Comforting rice bowls topped with tender chicken and sweet onions simmered in savoury dashi, finished with softly set egg that melts into the warm rice.
steps: Cook the rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it with the water in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes. Let it rest covered for 10 minutes.
Prepare chicken and onion: While the rice cooks, cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and slice the onion thinly.
Simmer the chicken: Bring dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a simmer in a wide pan. Add the onion and chicken and simmer for 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the eggs: Lightly beat the eggs so some white streaks remain. Pour two thirds over the chicken, cover for 1 minute, then add the rest and cook for 30 seconds until just set.
Serve: Fill four bowls with rice and slide the chicken and egg mixture on top with some of the broth. Garnish with sliced spring onions and a pinch of shichimi togarashi.

title: Pasta e Fagioli
description: A hearty, creamy Italian bean and pasta soup with pancetta, rosemary and tomato, the ultimate comforting one-pot dinner from the nonna's kitchen.
steps: Chop the vegetables: Finely dice the onion, carrot, celery and pancetta and slice the garlic. Drain and rinse the beans.

Blend partly: Remove the rosemary and blend about a third of the soup with a stick blender to make it creamy.
Cook the pasta in the soup: Add the ditalini and cook, stirring often, until al dente. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Rest and serve: Season, let it rest for 2 minutes, then serve with the remaining oil and the grated Parmigiano.

Let it soak: Leave the salad to stand for 15 minutes so the potatoes absorb the liquid, then fold in the oil and the thinly sliced cucumber.

description: Delicate Dover sole dusted in flour and pan-fried until golden, then bathed in nutty brown butter with lemon, capers and parsley, simple French elegance.

Finish the sauce: Take the pan off the heat and add the juice of one lemon, the capers and the chopped parsley.
Serve: Spoon the sizzling butter over the fish and serve with lemon wedges and boiled potatoes.

title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
description: Thin veal escalopes topped with prosciutto and fresh sage, pan-fried in butter and finished with a quick, glossy white wine sauce.

Dust with flour: Season lightly with pepper and very little salt, then dust the underside with flour.

title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crunchy panko-crusted chicken cutlets served with steamed rice and a mellow, thick Japanese curry sauce full of tender potatoes, carrots and sweet onions.
steps: Cook the rice: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and cook it with 400 ml water in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes. Let it rest covered for 10 minutes.
Start the curry: Cut the onions into wedges and the carrots and potatoes into bite-size chunks. Soften them in 1 tbsp oil in a large pot for 5 minutes.
Simmer the vegetables: Pour in 700 ml water, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Bread the chicken: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally and season with salt. Dust them in flour, dip in beaten egg and press firmly into the panko on both sides.
Thicken the curry: Take the pot off the heat, break in the curry roux and stir until dissolved. Return to low heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Fry the katsu: Heat the remaining oil in a deep frying pan to 170 °C. Fry the cutlets for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on a rack.
Plate up: Slice the katsu into strips and place next to a mound of rice. Spoon the curry sauce alongside and serve immediately so the crust stays crisp.

title: Coq au Vin
description: Chicken slowly braised in red wine with smoky bacon, glazed pearl onions and golden mushrooms until meltingly tender, a rustic Burgundian dish with deep, rich flavour.
steps: Brown bacon and chicken: Fry the lardons in a large casserole until crisp and remove them. Season the chicken and brown it in batches in the bacon fat until golden, then set aside.
Soften the vegetables: Cook the sliced carrots and chopped garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 1 more minute.
Braise in wine: Return the chicken and bacon, pour in the wine and stock, add the thyme and bring to a simmer. Cover and braise gently for 1 1/2 hours until the meat is tender.
Glaze the onions: Meanwhile, peel the pearl onions and cook them in half the butter with a splash of water until glazed and tender.
Sauté the mushrooms: Fry the quartered mushrooms in the remaining butter over high heat until browned, season them and set aside with the onions.
Reduce the sauce: Lift out the chicken and boil the sauce until it coats the back of a spoon. Stir in the onions and mushrooms and return the chicken to warm through.
Serve: Check the seasoning and serve the coq au vin with mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

title: Käsespätzle with Crispy Onions
description: Soft homemade egg noodles layered with melting Emmental and mountain cheese, crowned with a heap of crispy fried onions - Swabian comfort food at its best.
steps: Make the dough: Mix flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg and a teaspoon of salt and beat with a wooden spoon until the dough is smooth and forms bubbles. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Fry the onions: Slice the onions into thin rings and fry them slowly in half the butter over medium heat until deep golden and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.
Prepare water and cheese: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and preheat the oven to 180 °C. Coarsely grate both cheeses and mix them together.
Cook the spätzle: Press the dough in batches through a spätzle press, or scrape thin strips off a wet board, into the simmering water. Lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.
Layer with cheese: Layer the hot spätzle and the cheese in a dish greased with the remaining butter, seasoning each layer with a little pepper.
Melt and serve: Bake for about 8 minutes until the cheese has melted. Top with the crispy onions and chopped chives and serve at once.

title: Dal Tadka
description: Comforting yellow lentils simmered until creamy and crowned with a sizzling tempering of ghee, cumin, garlic and dried chilies, a humble everyday classic.
steps: Rinse the lentils: Rinse the lentils in a sieve under cold water several times until the water runs clear.
Cook the lentils: Bring the lentils, water, turmeric and a pinch of salt to the boil and skim off any foam. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and creamy.

Prepare the masala: While the lentils simmer, chop the onion, tomatoes and garlic. Fry the onion and ginger in 1 tbsp ghee for 6 minutes, add the tomatoes for 3 minutes and stir everything into the cooked lentils.
Make the tadka: Heat the remaining ghee in a small pan, add the cumin seeds, dried chilies and garlic and fry for about 1 minute until fragrant and golden.
Finish and serve: Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal, sprinkle with garam masala and chopped coriander and adjust the salt.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
description: Veal shanks braised slowly in white wine, tomato and vegetables until meltingly tender, finished with a zesty lemon, garlic and parsley gremolata.
steps: Prepare the shanks: Snip the membrane around each shank in a few places so they stay flat, season with salt and pepper and dust in flour.
Chop the vegetables: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery.
Brown the shanks: Heat the butter and oil in a wide casserole and brown the shanks well on both sides, then set them aside.
Build the sauce: Soften the vegetables in the same pot for 5 minutes, pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, then add the tomatoes and stock.
Braise: Return the shanks to the pot, cover and simmer very gently for about 1.5 hours, turning once, until the meat almost falls off the bone.
Make the gremolata: Finely chop the parsley and garlic and mix with the finely grated lemon zest.
Serve: Plate the shanks with plenty of sauce and sprinkle generously with gremolata. Serve with risotto or polenta.

title: Ramen Carbonara
description: Springy ramen noodles tossed in a silky Italian-style egg and Parmesan sauce with crispy pancetta, black pepper and a savoury splash of soy.

Mix the egg sauce: Whisk eggs, egg yolks, finely grated Parmesan, soy sauce and plenty of black pepper in a bowl.
Crisp the pancetta: Fry the diced pancetta in olive oil for 5 minutes until crisp, adding the sliced garlic for the last minute.
Cook the noodles: Cook the ramen noodles for 2-3 minutes until just tender, then drain and keep a cup of the cooking water.
Toss everything together: Take the pan off the heat, add the noodles to the pancetta and pour in the egg sauce with a splash of noodle water. Toss quickly until creamy, then top with spring onions.

title: Beef Bourguignon
description: Chunks of beef braised for hours in red Burgundy wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions until fork-tender, the ultimate slow-cooked French comfort classic.

title: Gyoza (Pan-fried Pork Dumplings)
description: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings with crispy golden bottoms and tender steamed tops, served with a tangy soy, rice vinegar and chili oil dip.
steps: Salt the cabbage: Chop the cabbage very finely, toss it with the salt and leave it for 10 minutes to draw out the water.
Prepare the aromatics: Finely chop the spring onions and grate the garlic and ginger.
Mix the dipping sauce: Stir 2 tbsp soy sauce with the rice vinegar and chili oil in a small bowl and set aside.
Make the filling: Squeeze the cabbage firmly to remove as much water as possible. Mix it with the pork, aromatics, remaining soy sauce and sesame oil, stirring for 1 minute until sticky.
Fold the first half: Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of a wrapper, wet the edge with water, fold it over and pleat one side to seal. Fold 16 gyoza and set them on a floured tray.
Fold the second half: At the same time, fold the remaining 16 gyoza the same way, keeping them apart so they do not stick together.

Pan-fry and steam: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan and fry half the gyoza flat side down for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Add 80 ml water, cover and steam for 4 minutes, then uncover until the water evaporates. Repeat with the second batch.
Serve: Turn the gyoza out crispy side up onto plates and serve hot with the dipping sauce.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice with Bacon

Fry the kimchi: Add the kimchi and gochujang to the bacon and fry for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Fry the rice: Add the cold rice, kimchi juice and soy sauce and stir-fry over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking up any lumps. Finish with the sesame oil.
Fry the eggs: In a second pan, fry the eggs in the vegetable oil until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Serve: Divide the rice between bowls, top each with an egg and sprinkle with spring onions and sesame seeds.

title: Pizza Margherita
description: The Neapolitan classic: a thin, airy homemade crust topped with bright San Marzano tomatoes, melting fior di latte mozzarella and fragrant fresh basil.
steps: Make the dough: Mix the flour, yeast and water, then add most of the salt and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let it rise: Cover the dough and leave it in a warm place for about 1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Prepare the sauce: Crush the tomatoes by hand and season with the remaining salt and half the olive oil. The sauce is not cooked.
Prep the toppings: Tear the mozzarella into pieces and let it drain in a sieve. Pick the basil leaves.
Heat the oven: Preheat the oven with a baking steel or upturned tray inside to its highest setting, ideally 250-275 °C.
Shape the pizzas: Divide the dough into 4 balls and stretch each by hand into a thin round with a slightly thicker rim.
Top and bake: Spread each base with sauce, scatter over the mozzarella and bake one or two at a time for 7-9 minutes until the crust is blistered.
Finish with basil: Top the hot pizzas with fresh basil and a drizzle of the remaining olive oil.

Finish with paneer: Stir in the cream and the fried paneer and heat through for 2 minutes before serving.

description: Crisp-skinned, rosy duck breast served with a glossy bittersweet orange sauce of caramel, citrus and Grand Marnier, the timeless French bistro classic.
steps: Score the duck: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Pat the duck breasts dry, score the skin in a fine crosshatch without cutting into the meat and season well with salt and pepper.
Render the skin: Place the breasts skin-side down in a cold pan, then turn the heat to medium and render slowly for 12-15 minutes until the skin is crisp and golden. Pour off the fat as it collects.
Make the caramel: Zest one orange and juice three of them. Cook the sugar in a small saucepan until it turns into an amber caramel, then carefully add the vinegar and stir until dissolved.
Finish the duck: Turn the breasts over, sear the flesh side for 2 minutes, then roast in the oven for 6-8 minutes until pink inside. Rest them on a board for 5 minutes.
Build the sauce: Add the orange juice, stock, thyme and Grand Marnier to the caramel and simmer until reduced by half. Thicken with the cornstarch mixed with a little cold water.
Mount the sauce: Remove the thyme, whisk in the cold butter and orange zest, then add segments of the remaining orange and season to taste.
Slice and serve: Slice the duck on the diagonal, fan it out on warm plates and spoon the orange sauce over it.

title: Tonkotsu-style Ramen (simplified)
description: A weeknight take on creamy tonkotsu ramen: rich garlic and sesame broth, tender braised pork belly, jammy soft-boiled eggs and springy noodles in every bowl.
steps: Braise the pork belly: Brown the pork belly on all sides in half of the oil in a small pot. Add 3 tbsp soy sauce, the mirin and the water, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, turning it now and then.
Soft-boil the eggs: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for exactly 6 and a half minutes. Cool them in ice water, peel and set aside.
Build the broth: Fry grated garlic and ginger in the remaining oil in a large pot for 1 minute, pour in the stock and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Make the broth creamy: Whisk in the soy milk, sesame paste and the remaining soy sauce and heat through without boiling. Season to taste with a splash of the pork braising liquid.
Slice the toppings: Lift out the pork and cut it into thin slices. Slice the spring onions, cut the nori into rectangles and halve the eggs lengthwise.
Cook the noodles: Boil the noodles in plenty of unsalted water for 1 to 2 minutes according to the packet, then drain them very well.
Assemble the bowls: Divide the noodles between four warm bowls and ladle over the hot broth. Top with pork slices, egg halves, spring onions and nori and serve straight away.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
description: Layers of tender pasta, slow-simmered beef and pancetta ragù and creamy béchamel, baked until bubbling with a golden Parmigiano crust.
steps: Chop the soffritto: Finely dice the onion, carrot, celery and pancetta.
Brown the meat: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and fry the pancetta and vegetables for 5 minutes. Add the minced beef and fry until browned and crumbly.
Simmer the ragù: Pour in the wine and let it bubble away, then stir in the passata, season and simmer gently with the lid ajar for about 1.5 hours, stirring now and then.
Make the béchamel: Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then add the milk little by little, whisking until smooth and thick. Season with salt and a pinch of nutmeg.
Prepare the dish: Grate the Parmigiano, butter a large baking dish and preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Layer the lasagne: Spread a little ragù in the dish, then add layers of pasta sheets, ragù, béchamel and Parmigiano. Repeat and finish with béchamel and a generous layer of cheese.
Bake: Bake for about 40 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
Rest and serve: Let the lasagne rest for 10 minutes so it holds together, then cut into portions.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken pieces grilled until lightly charred, then folded into a creamy, gently spiced tomato masala sauce that is a true curry-house favourite.
steps: Marinate the chicken: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and mix with the yogurt, half of each spice, one crushed garlic clove and a pinch of salt. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare the aromatics: While the chicken marinates, finely chop the onion and mince the remaining garlic. Keep the grated ginger ready next to the stove.
Grill the tikka: Spread the chicken on a lined baking tray and cook under a hot oven grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred.

Build the masala: Heat the oil in a deep pan and fry the onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger and remaining spices for 1 minute, then pour in the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cream: Stir the cream into the sauce and blend it with a stick blender if you like it extra smooth.
Simmer together: Add the grilled chicken to the sauce and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes. Season with salt and serve with rice or naan.

title: Sushi Burrito
description: A giant hand-held sushi roll wrapped in nori and packed with seasoned rice, fresh salmon, avocado, cucumber and a creamy sriracha mayo.
steps: Cook the rice: Rinse the sushi rice until the water runs clear, then simmer it with 480 ml water, covered, for 12 minutes and let it steam off the heat for 10 minutes.
Prep the fillings: Cut the salmon, avocados, cucumber and carrot into long thin strips. Keep the salmon chilled until needed.
Mix the sriracha mayo: Stir the mayonnaise with the sriracha until smooth and set it aside.
Season the rice: Dissolve sugar and salt in the rice vinegar and fold it gently through the warm rice. Spread it out to cool to room temperature.
Roll the burritos: Lay a nori sheet on a bamboo mat, spread a thin layer of rice over it and line up the fillings in the middle with some sriracha mayo. Roll up tightly like a burrito.
Slice and serve: Wrap each burrito half in baking paper, cut it in half with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce for dipping.

title: Rhineland Sauerbraten with Gingerbread Gravy
description: Tender beef braised slowly in a tangy red wine and vinegar marinade, finished with a glossy sweet-and-sour gingerbread gravy - Sunday lunch the Rhineland way.
steps: Make the marinade: Bring the wine, vinegar, 300 ml water, sliced onions, diced carrot, bay leaves, juniper berries and cloves to the boil. Pour the hot marinade over the beef in a snug bowl.
Marinate the beef: Leave the beef in the marinade for 30 minutes, turning it once. If you have time, marinate it covered in the fridge for up to 3 days for an even deeper flavour.
Brown the meat: Lift out the beef, pat it dry and season with salt and pepper. Brown it well on all sides in hot oil in a heavy casserole.
Braise slowly: Pour in the marinade with all the vegetables, cover and simmer gently over low heat for about 2 1/2 hours, turning the meat halfway, until fork-tender.
Strain the liquid: Lift out the beef and keep it warm under foil. Strain the braising liquid into a saucepan, pressing the soft vegetables through the sieve.
Finish the gravy: Crumble in the gingerbread, add the raisins and sugar and simmer, stirring, until the gravy is smooth and glossy. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Slice and serve: Slice the beef across the grain and serve with plenty of gravy, ideally with potato dumplings and red cabbage.

title: Beef Wellington
description: Tender beef fillet wrapped in savoury mushroom duxelles and prosciutto, baked in golden puff pastry for a show-stopping centrepiece that slices beautifully pink.
steps: Sear the beef: Season the beef tenderloin generously with salt and pepper and sear it on all sides in a very hot pan with the olive oil. Let it cool slightly, then brush it all over with Dijon mustard.

Make the duxelles: Finely chop the mushrooms, shallots and garlic. Cook them in the butter with the thyme leaves over medium-high heat until all the moisture has evaporated and the mixture is dry, then let it cool.

Wrap in prosciutto: Lay the prosciutto slices overlapping on a large sheet of cling film and spread the duxelles evenly over them. Place the beef on top and roll everything tightly into a log using the film.
Chill the roll: Chill the wrapped beef in the fridge for 20 minutes so it firms up and holds its shape.
Prepare the pastry: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Roll out the puff pastry to about 3 mm thick and whisk the egg yolk with a splash of water for the glaze.
Encase in pastry: Unwrap the beef, place it on the pastry and fold the pastry around it, sealing the edges and trimming any excess. Brush with egg wash and lightly score the top with a knife.
Bake: Bake on a lined tray for 35-40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and a thermometer reads 52 °C in the centre for medium-rare.
Rest and slice: Let the Wellington rest for 10 minutes, then cut it into thick slices with a sharp serrated knife.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Juicy pan-seared chicken thighs with crispy skin, lacquered in a glossy homemade soy, mirin and sake glaze and served over fluffy steamed rice.
steps: Cook the rice: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear, then cook it with the water in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it rest covered for 10 minutes.
Mix the teriyaki sauce: While the rice cooks, stir soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar has dissolved.
Prepare the chicken: Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper, season lightly with salt and prick the skin a few times with a fork so it stays flat.

Sear the chicken: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and lay the chicken in skin side down. Cook for 7 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp, then flip and cook for 4 more minutes.
Glaze the chicken: Wipe out most of the fat with kitchen paper, pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 3 to 4 minutes, spooning it over the chicken until thick and glossy.
Slice and serve: Rest the chicken for 2 minutes, slice it into strips and serve over the rice. Drizzle with the remaining glaze and sprinkle with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
description: Silky Roman spaghetti coated in a glossy sauce of egg yolks, Pecorino Romano and black pepper, studded with crisp, golden guanciale.
steps: Boil the water: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add the salt.
Crisp the guanciale: Cut the guanciale into short strips and fry it in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and the fat has rendered. Turn off the heat and leave it in the pan.
Make the egg cream: Whisk the egg yolks, the whole egg, both grated cheeses and most of the pepper in a bowl to a thick paste.
Cook the spaghetti: Cook the spaghetti until al dente. Scoop out a cup of pasta water before draining.

Combine off the heat: Toss the spaghetti in the guanciale pan, then take it off the heat and stir in the egg cream with a few splashes of pasta water until creamy and glossy. The eggs should thicken, not scramble.
Serve: Plate at once and finish with the remaining pepper and a little extra Pecorino.

title: Korean BBQ Tacos
description: Sweet and spicy gochujang-marinated beef seared hot and tucked into warm corn tortillas with crunchy quick-pickled slaw, sesame and fresh coriander.
steps: Marinate the beef: Slice the beef very thinly against the grain. Mix gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, grated garlic and half the sesame oil, then coat the beef and leave it for 15 minutes.
Make the quick slaw: Finely shred the red cabbage and grate the carrot. Toss with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt and let it soften while the beef marinates.
Prep the toppings: Slice the spring onions thinly and pick the coriander leaves. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Sear the beef: Heat the remaining sesame oil in a large pan over high heat. Fry the beef in two batches for 2-3 minutes until caramelised at the edges.
Warm the tortillas: Heat the tortillas in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side and keep them wrapped in a clean towel.
Assemble the tacos: Fill each tortilla with beef and slaw, then top with spring onions, coriander and sesame seeds. Serve right away.

title: Schweineschnitzel with Lemon and Parsley Potatoes
description: Thin pork cutlets in a golden, crackling breadcrumb crust, served with buttery parsley potatoes and a squeeze of fresh lemon - a true German favourite.
steps: Boil the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, halve any large ones and boil them in salted water for about 20 minutes until tender.
Pound the cutlets: Place the pork between two sheets of cling film and pound it to about 5 mm thick with a meat mallet or small pan. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Bread the cutlets: Put flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in three shallow plates. Coat each cutlet first in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, without pressing the crumbs down.

Fry the schnitzel: Heat the oil in a large pan until a breadcrumb sizzles immediately. Fry the cutlets for 2-3 minutes per side, gently swirling the pan so the crust puffs up, then drain on kitchen paper.
Toss the potatoes: Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot with the butter, chopped parsley and a pinch of salt. Toss gently until glossy.
Serve: Plate the schnitzel with the parsley potatoes and lemon wedges for squeezing over at the table.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Tender marinated chicken simmered in a velvety tomato, butter and cream sauce with warming garam masala and a hint of fenugreek, perfect with naan or basmati rice.
steps: Marinate the chicken: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and mix with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the chili powder, half the garam masala and a pinch of salt. Let it rest for 20 minutes.
Soften the onion: Finely chop the onion. Melt half the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion over medium heat for about 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Sear the chicken: Heat a large frying pan over high heat and sear the marinated chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned on all sides. It does not need to be cooked through yet.
Simmer the tomato sauce: Add the passata, sugar and the remaining chili powder and garam masala to the onion. Simmer for 12 minutes, then blend until smooth.

Combine and finish: Add the chicken to the sauce and stir in the cream, the remaining butter and the fenugreek leaves crushed between your palms. Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and season with salt.
